proposition: Under the map n -> n/2 when n is even, n -> 3n+1 when n is odd, every integer n with 1 <= n <= 562454 reaches 1 in fewer than 470 steps.
hypotheses: the stopping time counts steps until the value 1 is reached

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 50, the stopping time of n is less than 470.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 4910, the stopping time of n is less than 470.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n*(n+1) is congruent to (n*(n+1)) + 442 modulo 13.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, 2*n is at least n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n^2 + n is congruent to (n^2 + n) + 15 modulo 5.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, at least one of the following holds: n mod 3 = 0; n mod 3 = 1; n mod 3 = 2.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
The steps above establish the statement up to 4910, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 562454.
